messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person dinosaur photography game set in a forested river valley, with wildlife photography, photo sales, challenges, a nearby shop, and purchasable gear or vehicles.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- The repository had no existing game/app, so implementation is a self-contained static WebGL game without a package-based app stack.
- Use original procedural 3D geometry and browser-native controls; no external game engine dependency.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial game page and HUD/modal markup.
- Added responsive styling for start screen, HUD, shop, journal, and mobile controls.
- Implemented WebGL shader/geometry helpers, procedural forest/river/camp/shop/bridges, and dinosaur/wildlife meshes in `game.js`.
- Added initial gameplay data, shop inventory, photo-sales state, UI interactions, and desktop pointer/keyboard controls.

### Active
- Finish game loop: movement, rendering, wildlife aiming/photography, river hazards, mobile controls, HUD updates, and interaction prompts.
- Test the game in a browser and fix any runtime/visual issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue editing `game.js` with rendering, animation, movement, target detection, and touch controls.
2. Add styling for the new `.sell-row` shop element.
3. Run the project and verify gameplay visually and interactively.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game canvas, HUD, shop/journal/briefing markup.
- `game.js`: Current WebGL scene generation, creatures, state, and event handlers; still incomplete.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D first-person dinosaur photography game in a forested river valley, with wildlife photography, photo sales, challenges, a camp shop, and purchasable gear or vehicles.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Use a static WebGL game with original procedural geometry and browser-native controls; no package-based app stack or external game engine.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game page, responsive interface, procedural 3D world and wildlife, movement, photography, sales, shop inventory, objectives, journal, keyboard/pointer controls, and mobile controls.
- Fixed the `.vignette` gradient syntax that prevented most stylesheet rules from applying; added `.sell-row` styling.
- Verified start/briefing flow, shop opening, Trail boots purchase, camera targeting, photography, photo sales, and boots purchase in Chromium.
- Confirmed mobile viewport displays the joystick and action buttons; `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Finish gameplay QA for river crossings and mobile controls; investigate why synthetic touch input did not move the map.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Verify bridge and river crossings with keyboard movement; check raft behavior if practical.
2. Re-test mobile joystick, look-zone, and action buttons with reliable touch input; fix any issues found.
3. Briefly note assumptions when finishing.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game canvas, HUD, shop, journal, briefing, and mobile controls.
- `game.js`: WebGL world, game state, rendering, movement, photography, shop, and controls.
- `style.css`: Game visuals and responsive interface.

## Important Context
- Game files and scaffold files are uncommitted and currently untracked.
- Desktop Chromium targeting identified and photographed a Parasaurolophus; sales and the Trail boots purchase updated funds and inventory correctly.
- Mobile controls are visible at 390×844, but a synthetic CDP touch test left the player map position unchanged; the cause is unresolved.
- Earlier pointer-lock testing through an iframe did not work; direct CDP testing subsequently confirmed pointer lock and camera aiming.
